sections.h2: Who does what with a Boyle County tax bill
sections.html:
Three desks touch your bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), at 859-238-1104, decides what the property is worth for tax purposes and handles exemptions. The Sheriff's Office, at 321 W. Main Street, Room 103 in Danville (859-238-1123), mails the bills and takes payment. The County Clerk inherits any bill still open after the spring cutoff.

Valuing is never the sheriff's job. If the bill looks too large, talk to the PVA, and do it before you mail a check.

  • Value, exemptions, name or mailing address on the bill: PVA.
  • Paying this year's bill or looking it up: Sheriff's Office.
  • Bills from prior years: County Clerk.

Danville is the county seat, and Boyle County wraps around it in central Kentucky, with Junction City and Perryville as the other cities. The July 2025 population estimate is 31,632, up from 30,614 at the 2020 count. Owner-occupied houses are valued around $209,900 at the midpoint, and 68.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Typical rent is $778, and the county logged 94 building permits in 2025. That mix of steady demand and modest new construction is the market a seller faces.

Five cutoffs apply to each tax year. Below is the sheriff's schedule for the 2026 bills, where a postmark on or before the listed date counts.

Boyle County Sheriff's schedule for the 2026 bills
Paid or postmarked byAmount owed
November 30, 2026Face amount less a 2% discount
December 31, 2026Face amount
January 31, 2027Face amount plus a 5% penalty
April 15, 2027Face amount plus a 21% penalty
After April 15, 2027Handed to the County Clerk as delinquent

Every year repeats this pattern with the dates moved forward. The sheriff's Tax Bill Web Portal looks up bills by bill number, map number, owner or address. Searches by owner sometimes fail on reversed names, so try the last name first as well as the first name first.

sections.h2: Which school district bills Danville properties?
sections.html:
The answer changes from street to street. Danville Schools serve the city and Boyle County Schools serve the rest, yet some parcels within city limits belong to the county district. A Danville mailing address alone tells you nothing.

A parcel in the Danville Independent district gets its school bill straight from the school system at 859-936-8507. A parcel in the county district has school tax folded into the sheriff's bill. Library, health, fire and similar special districts show up as extra lines where they apply.

Danville's 2025 real property rate is 11.9 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 14.4 cents in 2017. The city says it has taken the compensating rate every year since 2017, so the rate slid while assessments grew.

  • Real property: 0.1190 in 2025, 0.1220 in 2024, 0.1440 in 2017.
  • Tangible personal property: 0.1595 in 2025.
  • Cars, trucks and boats: 0.2000 in 2025.

House Bill 44 lets a city hold revenue level with the compensating rate or raise it by up to 4 percent after a hearing. Past 4 percent, voters can petition to recall the increase. Your dollar total can still climb if the PVA raises the assessed value under a lower rate.

sections.h2: Can I contest my Boyle County assessment?
sections.html:
You can, though the PVA conference has to happen first and the state gives no shortcut. Property is valued as of January 1, and the public may inspect the roll for thirteen days in early May. Once the conference is over, take your appeal to the County Clerk before the workday ends on the day after inspection closes.

The county's board of assessment appeals meets roughly a month afterward and can sit up to five days. Arrive with proof, such as comparable sales, an appraisal, repair bids, insurance values or listings, because an appeal without it fails. Skip the local filing and the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

When the bills are printed before your dispute is settled, they use the value you claimed. A supplemental bill follows if the board sets it higher.

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or whom a public or private retirement system has classed as totally disabled, get a fixed deduction from the assessment on their residence. It tops out at $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Both ownership and residence must be true on January 1.

Send the application to the Boyle County PVA, the same office Danville points seniors toward. Get it in before December 31. Qualified but no exemption on the bill? Phone the PVA first, then pay.

sections.h2: Reading the lines on your bill
sections.html:
A Boyle County bill can hold more than one charge, and each has a different office behind it. County school tax is included on the sheriff's bill for parcels in the county district. Danville parcels in the independent district see their school charge come separately. Fire, library, health and other special districts appear as extra lines where they apply, and Danville city tax is figured at its own rate.

If a line looks wrong, ask which office set it. Value and exemption questions go to the PVA at 859-238-1104. Questions about the amount owed or the payment period go to the sheriff at 859-238-1123. Sorting that out early keeps a mistake from following you to the closing table, where the title company needs the numbers to be right.

sections.h2: When a Boyle County bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
Past April 15 the sheriff lets go of the bill. It turns into a certificate of delinquency held by the clerk, with a lien on the property. One percent interest is added each month, and commissions for the clerk and county attorney, postage and advertising stack on top. Within a week at the clerk's desk, the balance is well above what the sheriff would have taken.

Letters from the county attorney arrive at about 30 and 60 days. Unpaid certificates may be sold to outside buyers anywhere from 90 to 135 days after the handoff. If you are selling with old tax owing, request a payoff from the clerk and let the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell?
sections.html:
Kentucky bills whoever holds title on January 1. If your house changes hands in March, that year's bill still comes in your name. Closing agents normally split the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, then either pay the sheriff or credit whoever will. A lender with an escrow account does not get the bill automatically, so owners should forward it.

  1. Get the current figure from the sheriff.
  2. Get any older figure from the clerk.
  3. Give both to the closing agent before the closing date.
  4. Confirm on the settlement statement who pays and who gets a credit.

Houses that arrive through an estate, carry back taxes, or need repairs a retail buyer would balk at can sell directly to a cash buyer, who clears the tax at the same table.

faqs.q: Whom should I phone if my Boyle County assessment looks too high?
faqs.a: The PVA at 859-238-1104. The sheriff only collects, and the clerk handles appeal filings.

faqs.q: Is the Boyle County 2% discount still available after November?
faqs.a: No. On the 2026 bills the discount runs through November 30, 2026. December brings the face amount and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Do Danville homeowners get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: It varies. Parcels in the Danville Independent district get a separate school bill, while everything else, including Boyle County school tax, comes on the sheriff's bill.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: Up to $49,100 off the assessment through the 2026 tax year, for owner-occupants who are 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Boyle County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a payoff from the clerk for past-due years and a current figure from the sheriff, and the closing agent can pay both at closing.
